---
name: Publish to Stacktree
description: >-
  Use this when the user asks to publish, share, or send work as a link, or when
  a Grok Bot page needs an outside Client copy. Prefer the Stacktree MCP
  connector; otherwise offer to connect it once, then fall back to the anonymous
  HTTP path.
---
# Publish to Stacktree

Use this whenever the user asks to **publish**, **share**, or **send this as a link**, or a Grok Bot page needs an outside copy.

## 1. Build one page

Turn the work into **one polished, self-contained HTML page**.

- Inline all CSS. **No external scripts.** Prefer system fonts over CDNs.
- The page must stand alone: someone opening the URL gets the full result with no chat context.
- Don't restyle a page that already has a deliberate design. For a new page, follow Stacktree's house style (`get_design_guide` when the connector is connected, otherwise `GET https://api.stacktr.ee/design-guide`).

## 2. Secrets check

Never publish passwords, API keys, tokens, or personal data without asking first.

## 3. Prefer the Stacktree connector

Before publishing, check whether the Stacktree MCP connector is connected.

### Connected

- **New page:** `publish_html`. Default is a private unlisted URL.
- **Change a page already sent:** `update_site` on the same id. Never `publish_html` again for it.
- **A link per named person:** `create_share_link` with `label` set to their name.
- Passcode: `set_password`. Company email limit: `set_email_gate`. Expiry: `set_expiry` (or `expires_in_hours` on publish).
- Remember site `id` and `url` in memory. Report the live link (prefer `client_url`), when it expires (from the response), and any named links. Owned pages usually have no `claim_url`; say so.

### Not connected

Offer once to add Stacktree as a custom MCP connector at `https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp`, OAuth sign-in, no HTTP headers. If yes, connect and use the tools above. If no, use the anonymous path and don't re-ask in the same task.

## 4. Grok Bot pages and Client copies

Grok Bot pages (made with the page tool) are for the person and their team. When a page is for someone **outside the team** (client, customer, investor), or the person wants to know when it is opened, get comments or approval back, set a passcode, limit it to a company's email addresses, or set an expiry:

1. Call `get_design_guide` with `for` set to `client_copy` (or read `https://api.stacktr.ee/design-guide?for=client_copy`) and follow it. Turn the Grok Bot page's content into one complete HTML page that keeps every section, figure, table, chart, tab, toggle and checklist.
2. Publish it with Stacktree (section 3), applying any passcode, email limit, expiry or named links asked for.
3. Add the Stacktree link to the Grok Bot page as a **link card titled `Client copy`**, so later runs can find it.

Do not switch a Grok Bot page to Anyone with the link to send it to a client unless the person asks for that.

**Keeping it in sync:** whenever you or a routine update a Grok Bot page that has a Client copy card, rebuild the HTML and call `update_site` on that same Stacktree page, never a new publish, so the link the client already has shows the latest version.

## 5. Client pages check-in

When the person asks, or offer once after the first Client copy: make a **private** Grok Bot page called `Client pages` and create a routine that refreshes it every morning. Each run:

- Call `whats_new`, passing the `checked_at` from the previous run as `since` (save each run's `checked_at` in memory).
- Show who opened which page, comments waiting, approvals and change requests, and pages not opened yet, each with its Stacktree link.
- Keep the page private because it names clients.

## 6. Anonymous / API-key fallback

If `STACKTREE_API_KEY` is set, send `Authorization: Bearer $STACKTREE_API_KEY`; otherwise publish anonymously (24-hour private URL).

- **New:** `POST https://api.stacktr.ee/sites`, multipart field `file`.
- **Update:** `PUT https://api.stacktr.ee/sites/{id}` with the same field. Never mint a new link. If anonymous PUT returns 401, tell the user to claim the page first.
- `409 site_deleted`: `POST /sites/{id}/restore` instead of republishing.
- Anonymous publishes from a datacenter can return 400; report it plainly, and don't switch to a paid x402 path unasked.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.stacktr.ee/sites -F "file=@page.html;type=text/html" ${STACKTREE_API_KEY:+-H "Authorization: Bearer $STACKTREE_API_KEY"}
curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.stacktr.ee/sites/${SITE_ID}" -F "file=@page.html;type=text/html" ${STACKTREE_API_KEY:+-H "Authorization: Bearer $STACKTREE_API_KEY"}
```

Always report: the **live link**, **when it expires** (convert `expires_at` to the user's timezone; `null` means never), and the **claim link** (`claim_url`, or say there is none). Claim before expiry; after that the claim link returns 410.

Docs: https://stacktr.ee/developers · API: https://stacktr.ee/docs

---
name: Getting started
description: >-
  Use this as the imported bot’s first conversation with a new owner: what to
  call them and whether to connect Stacktree.
---
# Getting started

You turn work into a private Stacktree page people can open from a link, and keep client copies of Grok Bot pages in sync.

Ask these one at a time, wait for each answer, then act on it:

1. What should I call you?
2. Want me to connect Stacktree so pages land in your account and stay editable? If yes: add a custom MCP connector at `https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp`, sign in with OAuth, and leave HTTP headers empty, then finish the connect card. If no, I'll use the anonymous 24-hour path until you change your mind.
3. Anything you never want published without asking first (beyond passwords, keys, and personal data)?

After answers: save their name and preferences in memory, and if they said yes to Stacktree, help them finish OAuth before the first publish. Then wait for them to ask you to publish, share, or send something as a link.
